newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Economists revise down Sweden CPI outlook.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Economists revise down Sweden CPI outlook.

text.p: Several economists are lowering their forecasts for Swedish inflation for calendar 1996 after figures on Thursday showed a greater-than-expected drop in consumer prices in August.
"We will most likely lower our forecast to 0.9 percent at the end of the year from 1.3 percent," Peter Lindquist, economist at HSBC Midland, told Reuters.
Inflation in Sweden has fallen continuously from its latest peak of 3.3 percent in April 1995.
Figures released on Thursday by Statistics Sweden showed a 0.4 percent drop in consumer prices in August for a year-on-year rise of 0.3 percent, its lowest since 1959.
A Reuters poll had found the market expected consumer prices to be flat in August for a year-on-year rise of 0.7 percent.
"It has been quite low since January anyway. The only negative surprise was the April figure. But we didn't think it would be this low," said Olle Djerf, economist at Nordbanken.
Nordbanken made its latest economic forecast on August 29 when it saw inflation at 1.2 percent for the year.
Djerf said the bank would now lower its forecast to 1.0 percent. But he said he still thought inflation would rise in the coming 12 months.
"It is unlikely that rates will continue to fall at the same pace or that the crown will continue to strengthen at the same rate as over the past year," he said.
Knut Hallberg, economist at Swedbank, was more hesitant to revise his inflation forecast. Swedbank's latest inflation forecast on September 3 put inflation at 1.2 percent for 1996.
"You have to consider all problems before you can make any comment on the overall picture," he said.
"We don't know for example what structural changes have been made in the grocery sector and how that has affected competition."
He said it was hard to say what effect this would have and how much prices would move.
"If a decrease in grocery prices depends on increased competition, it increases the Riksbank's possibilities of keeping the repo rate low even if the economy picks up," Hallberg said.

Much of the fall in consumer prices in August was explained by normal seasonal price falls of fresh vegetables and fruit which together with meat prices reduced the consumer price level by 0.2 percent in August from July.
Lower gasoline prices accounted for 0.1 percent and lower costs for home owners for 0.1 percent, partly because of techical factors.

On Wednesday this week a survey commissioned by the Riksbank showed Sweden's business sector had lowered its inflationary expectations over the past three months to below the central bank's own goals.

Research institute Prospera found money market players, purchasing managers, employees' and employers' organisations now on average saw inflation at an annualised 1.7 percent in a year's time against expectations of 2.3 percent in a May poll.
The Riksbank has set a target of two percent annual inflation for the next two years.
-- Barbara Taltavull, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1019
